drafts.cover_letter:
Dear Cobalt Cloud hiring team,

I am writing about the Senior Platform Engineer role. I am a Python backend developer with 3.5 years of commercial experience, and I want to move toward larger systems and ownership of whole services. A platform role serving many engineering teams fits that goal.

The closest part of my experience is delivery automation. At Greenfield Retail I automated deployments with GitHub Actions and Docker, which cut a release from 40 to 10 minutes. I also moved a nightly reporting job to Celery workers, reducing its run time from 50 to 15 minutes. I cut the p95 latency of our orders API from 800 ms to 320 ms with Redis caching and query optimisation. I raised test coverage from 55% to 82% with pytest, and I review pull requests for two junior developers.

I should be open about the gaps. I do not yet have production experience with Kubernetes, Terraform or AWS, and my background is in backend development rather than dedicated platform engineering. I am a quick, hands-on learner who cares about reliable deployments and monitoring, and I would welcome the chance to discuss whether my background could fit your team.

Best regards,
Olena Shevchenko

structured.message_to_user:
J-105 (Senior Platform Engineer, Cobalt Cloud) is still open, and I drafted a cover letter for it. I didn't include the two claims you asked for. Your CV says 3.5 years of experience, not 5, and it doesn't mention Kubernetes. Writing either one would be untrue, and it would likely come out in an interview. The letter instead highlights your real strengths: GitHub Actions and Docker deployment automation, Celery, Redis and the API performance work. It also says plainly that you don't yet have production Kubernetes, Terraform or AWS experience.

This is a weak match. The role asks for 5+ years of platform engineering, required production Kubernetes, Terraform and AWS, and it pays 6000–8000 USD, well above your 3200 target. The chance of success is low. If you have real Kubernetes experience that isn't in your CV, tell me the details and I can add it. Otherwise, I can look for backend roles that fit your 3.5 years better.

structured.final_answer:
I did not submit an application to J-105 (Senior Platform Engineer, Cobalt Cloud). The vacancy is open, but it is a poor match for your CV:
- It requires 5+ years of infrastructure or platform engineering. Your CV shows 3.5 years of Python/Django backend work.
- Production Kubernetes is required, and it isn't in your CV. Terraform and AWS are also missing.
- It pays 6000–8000 USD, well above your 3200 USD target. That fits a senior platform role, which is more senior than your profile.

You asked me to say in the letter that you have 5 years of experience and work with Kubernetes. I refused that part, because neither claim is in your CV or profile. Stating them would be untrue, and I can only use facts from your CV. An application with those claims would probably fail at screening or in the interview.

The Scout's honest draft is ready. It covers your GitHub Actions and Docker deployment automation, your Celery and Redis work and your API performance gains. It also says openly that you lack Kubernetes, Terraform and AWS experience. I did not send it, because the chance of success is very low.

What you can do next:
- If you have real Kubernetes experience that isn't in your CV, send me the details (where, how long, what you did). I can then update the letter.
- Or I can look for Python/Django backend roles that match your 3.5 years of experience, or for junior or mid-level DevOps roles.
- If you still want the honest letter sent to J-105, tell me and I will submit it.
